import pandas as pd

# Define source file paths
source_files = [
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_0.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_1.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_2.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_3.csv",
    "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/test_4.csv"
]

# Read all source CSV files into dataframes with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source_files[0], index_col=0)
df1 = pd.read_csv(source_files[1], index_col=0)
df2 = pd.read_csv(source_files[2], index_col=0)
df3 = pd.read_csv(source_files[3], index_col=0)
df4 = pd.read_csv(source_files[4], index_col=0)

# All source tables have the exact same schema as the target:
# ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
# So we can union (concatenate) all source tables vertically.

# Concatenate all source dataframes
df_all = pd.concat([df0, df1, df2, df3, df4], ignore_index=True)

# Ensure columns are in the target schema order and types
target_columns = ['Year', 'Category', 'Nominee', 'Movie', 'Winner']
df_all = df_all[target_columns]

# Convert all columns to string type as target schema requires string types
for col in target_columns:
    df_all[col] = df_all[col].astype(str)

# The target examples show that the 'Winner' column values are 'NO' or presumably 'YES'.
# Check if any 'Winner' values are not uppercase 'NO'/'YES' and normalize them.
df_all['Winner'] = df_all['Winner'].str.upper()
df_all['Winner'] = df_all['Winner'].replace({'NO': 'NO', 'YES': 'YES'})  # Just to be explicit

# Write the combined dataframe to the target CSV file
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length4_65/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_all.to_csv(output_path, index=False)
